1.sahih_international: By those [angels] who extract with violence
1.pickthall: By those who drag forth to destruction,
1.yusuf_ali: By the (angels) who tear out (the souls of the wicked) with violence;
1.shakir: I swear by the angels who violently pull out the souls of the wicked,
1.muhammad_sarwar: By the angels who violently tear-out the souls of the disbelievers from their bodies,
1.mohsin_khan: By those (angels) who pull out (the souls of the disbelievers and the wicked) with great violence;
1.arberry: By those that pluck out vehemently

2.sahih_international: And [by] those who remove with ease
2.yusuf_ali: By those who gently draw out (the souls of the blessed);
2.shakir: And by those who gently draw out the souls of the blessed,
2.muhammad_sarwar: by the angels who gently release the souls of the believers,
2.mohsin_khan: By those (angels) who gently take out (the souls of the believers);
2.arberry: and those that draw out violently,

3.sahih_international: And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming
3.yusuf_ali: And by those who glide along (on errands of mercy),
3.shakir: And by those who float in space,
3.muhammad_sarwar: by the angels who float (in the heavens by the will of God),
3.mohsin_khan: And by those that swim along (i.e. angels or planets in their orbits, etc.).

4.sahih_international: And those who race each other in a race
4.yusuf_ali: Then press forward as in a race,
4.shakir: Then those who are foremost going ahead,
4.muhammad_sarwar: by the angels who hasten along
4.mohsin_khan: And by those that press forward as in a race (i.e. the angels or stars or the horses, etc.).

5.pickthall: And those who govern the event,
5.yusuf_ali: Then arrange to do (the Commands of their Lord),
5.shakir: Then those who regulate the affair.
5.muhammad_sarwar: and by the angels who regulate the affairs, (you will certainly be resurrected).
5.mohsin_khan: And by those angels who arrange to do the Commands of their Lord, (so verily, you disbelievers will be called to account).
5.arberry: by those that direct an affair!

6.sahih_international: On the Day the blast [of the Horn] will convulse [creation],
6.pickthall: On the day when the first trump resoundeth.
6.yusuf_ali: One Day everything that can be in commotion will be in violent commotion,
6.shakir: The day on which the quaking one shall quake,
6.muhammad_sarwar: On the day when the first trumpet sound blasts
6.mohsin_khan: On the Day (when the first blowing of the Trumpet is blown), the earth and the mountains will shake violently (and everybody will die),
6.arberry: Upon the day when the first blast shivers

7.sahih_international: There will follow it the subsequent [one].
7.shakir: What must happen afterwards shall follow it.
7.muhammad_sarwar: and will be followed by the second one,
7.mohsin_khan: The second blowing of the Trumpet follows it (and everybody will be raised up),
7.arberry: and the second blast follows it,

8.pickthall: On that day hearts beat painfully
8.yusuf_ali: Hearts that Day will be in agitation;
8.shakir: Hearts on that day shall palpitate,
8.mohsin_khan: (Some) hearts that Day will shake with fear and anxiety.
8.arberry: hearts upon that day shall be athrob

9.yusuf_ali: Cast down will be (their owners') eyes.
9.muhammad_sarwar: and eyes will be humbly cast down.
9.arberry: and their eyes shall be humbled.

10.sahih_international: They are [presently] saying, "Will we indeed be returned to [our] former state [of life]?
10.pickthall: (Now) they are saying: Shall we really be restored to our first state
10.yusuf_ali: They say (now): "What! shall we indeed be returned to (our) former state?
10.shakir: They say: Shall we indeed be restored to (our) first state?
10.muhammad_sarwar: (The disbelievers) say, "Shall we be brought back to life again
10.mohsin_khan: They say: "Shall we indeed be returned to (our) former state of life?
10.arberry: They shall say, 'What, are we being restored as we were before?

11.sahih_international: Even if we should be decayed bones?
11.pickthall: Even after we are crumbled bones?
11.yusuf_ali: "What! - when we shall have become rotten bones?"
11.shakir: What! when we are rotten bones?
11.muhammad_sarwar: after we have become bones and dust?"
11.arberry: What, when we are bones old and wasted?'

12.sahih_international: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."
12.pickthall: They say: Then that would be a vain proceeding.
12.yusuf_ali: They say: "It would, in that case, be a return with loss!"
12.shakir: They said: That then would be a return occasioning loss.
12.muhammad_sarwar: They have said, "Such a resurrection will certainly be a great loss".
12.mohsin_khan: They say: "It would in that case, be a return with loss!"
12.arberry: They shall say, 'That then were a losing return!'

13.sahih_international: Indeed, it will be but one shout,
13.pickthall: Surely it will need but one shout,
13.yusuf_ali: But verily, it will be but a single (Compelling) Cry,
13.shakir: But it shall be only a single cry,
13.muhammad_sarwar: However, it will only take a single blast
13.mohsin_khan: But only, it will be a single Zajrah [shout (i.e., the second blowing of the Trumpet)]. (See Verse 37:19).
13.arberry: But it shall be only a single scare,

14.sahih_international: And suddenly they will be [alert] upon the earth's surface.
14.pickthall: And lo! they will be awakened.
14.yusuf_ali: When, behold, they will be in the (full) awakening (to Judgment).
14.shakir: When lo! they shall be wakeful.
14.muhammad_sarwar: to bring them out of their graves and back to life on the earth's surface.
14.mohsin_khan: When, behold, they find themselves over the earth alive after their death,

15.sahih_international: Has there reached you the story of Moses? -
15.pickthall: Hath there come unto thee the history of Moses?
15.yusuf_ali: Has the story of Moses reached thee?
15.shakir: Has not there come to you the story of Musa?
15.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), have you heard the story of Moses
15.mohsin_khan: Has there come to you the story of Musa (Moses)?
15.arberry: Hast thou received the story of Moses?

16.sahih_international: When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa,
16.pickthall: How his Lord called him in the holy vale of Tuwa,
16.yusuf_ali: Behold, thy Lord did call to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa:-
16.shakir: When his Lord called upon him in the holy valley, twice,
16.muhammad_sarwar: when his Lord called him in the holy valley of Tuwa,
16.mohsin_khan: When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa,
16.arberry: When his Lord called to him in the holy valley, Towa:

17.sahih_international: "Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
17.pickthall: (Saying:) Go thou unto Pharaoh - Lo! he hath rebelled -
17.yusuf_ali: "Go thou to Pharaoh for he has indeed transgressed all bounds:
17.shakir: Go to Firon, surely he has become inordinate.
17.muhammad_sarwar: saying, "Go to the Pharaoh. He has transgressed beyond all bounds.
17.mohsin_khan: Go to Fir'aun (Pharaoh), verily, he has transgressed all bounds (in crimes, sins, polytheism, disbelief, etc.).
17.arberry: 'Go to Pharaoh; he has waxed insolent.

18.sahih_international: And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself
18.pickthall: And say (unto him): Hast thou (will) to grow (in grace)?
18.yusuf_ali: "And say to him, 'Wouldst thou that thou shouldst be purified (from sin)?-
18.shakir: Then say: Have you (a desire) to purify yourself:
18.muhammad_sarwar: And say to him, "Would you like to reform yourself?
18.mohsin_khan: And say to him: "Would you purify yourself (from the sin of disbelief by becoming a believer)",
18.arberry: And say, "Hast thou the will to purify thyself;

19.sahih_international: And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'"
19.pickthall: Then I will guide thee to thy Lord and thou shalt fear (Him).
19.yusuf_ali: "'And that I guide thee to thy Lord, so thou shouldst fear Him?'"
19.shakir: And I will guide you to your Lord so that you should fear.
19.muhammad_sarwar: I shall guide you to your Lord so that you may perhaps have fear of Him".
19.mohsin_khan: And that I guide you to your Lord, so you should fear Him?
19.arberry: and that I should guide thee to thy Lord, then thou shalt fear?"'

20.sahih_international: And he showed him the greatest sign,
20.pickthall: And he showed him the tremendous token.
20.yusuf_ali: Then did (Moses) show him the Great Sign.
20.shakir: So he showed him the mighty sign.
20.muhammad_sarwar: Moses showed him the great miracle
20.mohsin_khan: Then [Musa (Moses)] showed him the great sign (miracles).
20.arberry: So he showed him the great sign,

21.shakir: But he rejected (the truth) and disobeyed.
21.muhammad_sarwar: but the Pharaoh rejected it and disobeyed (Moses).
21.arberry: but he cried lies, and rebelled,

22.sahih_international: Then he turned his back, striving.
22.pickthall: Then turned he away in haste,
22.yusuf_ali: Further, he turned his back, striving hard (against Allah).
22.muhammad_sarwar: Then he turned away in a hurry,
22.mohsin_khan: Then he turned his back, striving hard (against Allah).

23.sahih_international: And he gathered [his people] and called out
23.yusuf_ali: Then he collected (his men) and made a proclamation,
23.shakir: Then he gathered (men) and called out.
23.mohsin_khan: Then he gathered his people and cried aloud,

24.sahih_international: And said, "I am your most exalted lord."
24.pickthall: And proclaimed: "I (Pharaoh) am your Lord the Highest."
24.yusuf_ali: Saying, "I am your Lord, Most High".
24.shakir: Then he said: I am your lord, the most high.
24.mohsin_khan: Saying: "I am your lord, most high",
24.arberry: and proclaimed, and he said, 'I am your Lord, the Most High!'

25.sahih_international: So Allah seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression].
25.pickthall: So Allah seized him (and made him) an example for the after (life) and for the former.
25.yusuf_ali: But Allah did punish him, (and made an) example of him, - in the Hereafter, as in this life.
25.shakir: So Allah seized him with the punishment of the hereafter and the former life.
25.muhammad_sarwar: So God struck him with the torment of this life and the life hereafter.
25.mohsin_khan: So Allah, seized him with punishment for his last [i.e. his saying: "I am your lord, most high") (see Verse 79:24)] and first [(i.e. his saying, "O chiefs! I know not that you have a god other than I" (see Verse 28:38)] transgression.
25.arberry: So God seized him with the chastisement of the Last World and the First.

26.sahih_international: Indeed in that is a warning for whoever would fear [Allah].
26.pickthall: Lo! herein is indeed a lesson for him who feareth.
26.yusuf_ali: Verily in this is an instructive warning for whosoever feareth (Allah).
26.shakir: Most surely there is in this a lesson to him who fears.
26.muhammad_sarwar: In this there is a lesson for those who have fear of God.
26.mohsin_khan: Verily, in this is an instructive admonition for whosoever fears Allah.
26.arberry: Surely in that is a lesson for him who fears!

27.sahih_international: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? Allah constructed it.
27.pickthall: Are ye the harder to create, or is the heaven that He built?
27.yusuf_ali: What! Are ye the more difficult to create or the heaven (above)? (Allah) hath constructed it:
27.shakir: Are you the harder to create or the heaven? He made it.
27.muhammad_sarwar: (People), is your creation harder for God than that of the heavens, which He created, raised and established
27.mohsin_khan: Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven that He constructed?
27.arberry: What, are you stronger in constitution or the heaven He built?

28.sahih_international: He raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
28.pickthall: He raised the height thereof and ordered it;
28.yusuf_ali: On high hath He raised its canopy, and He hath given it order and perfection.
28.shakir: He raised high its height, then put it into a right good state.
28.mohsin_khan: He raised its height, and He has equally ordered it,
28.arberry: He lifted up its vault, and levelled it,

29.sahih_international: And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.
29.pickthall: And He made dark the night thereof, and He brought forth the morn thereof.
29.yusuf_ali: Its night doth He endow with darkness, and its splendour doth He bring out (with light).
29.shakir: And He made dark its night and brought out its light.
29.muhammad_sarwar: He has made its nights dark and its days bright.
29.mohsin_khan: Its night He covers with darkness, and its forenoon He brings out (with light).
29.arberry: and darkened its night, and brought forth its forenoon;

30.sahih_international: And after that He spread the earth.
30.pickthall: And after that He spread the earth,
30.yusuf_ali: And the earth, moreover, hath He extended (to a wide expanse);
30.shakir: And the earth, He expanded it after that.
30.muhammad_sarwar: After this, He spread out the earth,
30.mohsin_khan: And after that He spread the earth;
30.arberry: and the earth-after that He spread it out,

31.sahih_international: He extracted from it its water and its pasture,
31.pickthall: And produced therefrom the water thereof and the pasture thereof,
31.yusuf_ali: He draweth out therefrom its moisture and its pasture;
31.shakir: He brought forth from it its water and its pasturage.
31.mohsin_khan: And brought forth therefrom its water and its pasture;
31.arberry: therefrom brought forth its waters and its pastures,

32.sahih_international: And the mountains He set firmly
32.pickthall: And He made fast the hills,
32.yusuf_ali: And the mountains hath He firmly fixed;-
32.shakir: And the mountains, He made them firm,
32.mohsin_khan: And the mountains He has fixed firmly;
32.arberry: and the mountains He set firm,

33.sahih_international: As provision for you and your grazing livestock.
33.pickthall: A provision for you and for your cattle.
33.yusuf_ali: For use and convenience to you and your cattle.
33.shakir: A provision for you and for your cattle.
33.muhammad_sarwar: All this was done as a means of enjoyment for you and your cattle.
33.mohsin_khan: (To be) a provision and benefit for you and your cattle.
33.arberry: an enjoyment for you and your flocks.

34.sahih_international: But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity -
34.pickthall: But when the great disaster cometh,
34.yusuf_ali: Therefore, when there comes the great, overwhelming (Event),-
34.shakir: But when the great predominating calamity comes;
34.muhammad_sarwar: On the day when the great calamity comes,
34.mohsin_khan: But when there comes the greatest catastrophe (i.e. the Day of Recompense, etc.),
34.arberry: Then, when the Great Catastrophe comes

35.sahih_international: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove,
35.pickthall: The day when man will call to mind his (whole) endeavour,
35.yusuf_ali: The Day when man shall remember (all) that he strove for,
35.shakir: The day on which man shall recollect what he strove after,
35.muhammad_sarwar: the human being will recall whatever he has done.
35.mohsin_khan: The Day when man shall remember what he strove for,
35.arberry: upon the day when man shall remember what he has striven,

36.sahih_international: And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see -
36.pickthall: And hell will stand forth visible to him who seeth,
36.yusuf_ali: And Hell-Fire shall be placed in full view for (all) to see,-
36.shakir: And the hell shall be made manifest to him who sees
36.muhammad_sarwar: Hell fire will become visible for those who would see it.
36.mohsin_khan: And Hell-fire shall be made apparent in full view for (every) one who sees,
36.arberry: and Hell is advanced for whoever sees,

37.sahih_international: So as for he who transgressed
37.pickthall: Then, as for him who rebelled
37.yusuf_ali: Then, for such as had transgressed all bounds,
37.shakir: Then as for him who is inordinate,
37.mohsin_khan: Then, for him who Tagha (transgressed all bounds, in disbelief, oppression and evil deeds of disobedience to Allah).
37.arberry: then as for him who was insolent

38.sahih_international: And preferred the life of the world,
38.pickthall: And chose the life of the world,
38.yusuf_ali: And had preferred the life of this world,
38.shakir: And prefers the life of this world,
38.mohsin_khan: And preferred the life of this world (by following his evil desires and lusts),

39.sahih_international: Then indeed, Hellfire will be [his] refuge.
39.pickthall: Lo! hell will be his home.
39.shakir: Then surely the hell, that is the abode.
39.mohsin_khan: Verily, his abode will be Hell-fire;
39.arberry: surely Hell shall be the refuge.

40.sahih_international: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,
40.pickthall: But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust,
40.yusuf_ali: And for such as had entertained the fear of standing before their Lord's (tribunal) and had restrained (their) soul from lower desires,
40.shakir: And as for him who fears to stand in the presence of his Lord and forbids the soul from low desires,
40.muhammad_sarwar: However, those who had feared their Lord and restrained their souls from acting according to its desires.
40.mohsin_khan: But as for him who feared standing before his Lord, and restrained himself from impure evil desires, and lusts.
40.arberry: But as for him who feared the Station of his Lord and forbade the soul its caprice,

41.sahih_international: Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.
41.pickthall: Lo! the Garden will be his home.
41.yusuf_ali: Their abode will be the Garden.
41.shakir: Then surely the garden-- that is the abode.
41.mohsin_khan: Verily, Paradise will be his abode.
41.arberry: surely Paradise shall be the refuge.

42.sahih_international: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?
42.pickthall: They ask thee of the Hour: when will it come to port?
42.yusuf_ali: They ask thee about the Hour,-'When will be its appointed time?
42.shakir: They ask you about the hour, when it will come.
42.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), they ask you, "When will the Hour of Doom come?"
42.mohsin_khan: They ask you (O Muhammad (Peace be upon him)) about the Hour, - when will be its appointed time?
42.arberry: They will question thee concerning the Hour, when it shall berth.

43.sahih_international: In what [position] are you that you should mention it?
43.pickthall: Why (ask they)? What hast thou to tell thereof?
43.yusuf_ali: Wherein art thou (concerned) with the declaration thereof?
43.shakir: About what! You are one to remind of it.
43.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), you do not know (when and how) it will come.
43.mohsin_khan: You have no knowledge to say anything about it,
43.arberry: What art thou about, to mention it?

44.sahih_international: To your Lord is its finality.
44.pickthall: Unto thy Lord belongeth (knowledge of) the term thereof.
44.yusuf_ali: With thy Lord in the Limit fixed therefor.
44.shakir: To your Lord is the goal of it.
44.muhammad_sarwar: This matter is in the hands of your Lord.
44.mohsin_khan: To your Lord belongs (the knowledge of) the term thereof?
44.arberry: Unto thy Lord is the final end of it.

45.sahih_international: You are only a warner for those who fear it.
45.pickthall: Thou art but a warner unto him who feareth it.
45.yusuf_ali: Thou art but a Warner for such as fear it.
45.shakir: You are only a warner to him who would fear it.
45.muhammad_sarwar: You are only a warner for those who fear such a day.
45.mohsin_khan: You (O Muhammad (Peace be upon him)) are only a warner for those who fear it,
45.arberry: Thou art only the warner of him who fears it.

46.sahih_international: It will be, on the Day they see it, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.
46.pickthall: On the day when they behold it, it will be as if they had but tarried for an evening or the morn thereof.
46.yusuf_ali: The Day they see it, (It will be) as if they had tarried but a single evening, or (at most till) the following morn!
46.shakir: On the day that they see it, it will be as though they had not tarried but the latter part of a day or the early part of it.
46.muhammad_sarwar: On the day when they see it, it will seem to them as though they had only lived in the world for a morning and an afternoon.
46.mohsin_khan: The Day they see it, (it will be) as if they had not tarried (in this world) except an afternoon or a morning.
46.arberry: It shall be as if; on the day they see it, they have but tarried for an evening, or its forenoon.
